From: Ellie Park <ellie@dataops.ai>
To: mina_haddad@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 4 Sep 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Pricing inquiry — match request and migration concerns

Hi Mina,

Thanks for taking my initial call earlier. We currently have an incumbent inference provider (EdgeServe) offering us a blended rate that is ~25% lower than Redwood's published list for comparable runtime credits. Before we kick off any formal procurement, I wanted to check: would Redwood be open to a price-match + migration credit if we commit to a 12-month reserved capacity?

Key constraints from our side:
- Zero downtime during peak nightly batch windows (00:00–03:00 PT)
- Data residency in AWS us-west-2
- Need to validate that model-compatibility (LLama-derived family + custom quantized checkpoints) will run without retraining or heavy conversion work

I've attached a simple usage snapshot (Q4_usage_estimate.csv) so you can see the mix. If you can share a rough commercial framework and a migration/ops checklist that calls out expected downtime and conversion effort, that would help speed internal approval.

Thanks,
Ellie
Ellie Park
Head of Platform Engineering
DataOps.ai

Attachment: Q4_usage_estimate.csv (CSV, 12 KB)

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Ellie Park <ellie@dataops.ai>
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 4 Sep 2026 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing inquiry — match request and migration concerns

Hi Ellie — great to connect. Appreciate the usage snapshot; that helps.

Short answers up front: yes, we have a commercially scoped price-match path for qualified deals and we can offer migration credits to offset cutover engineering. What varies is the technical effort (mostly on the model conversion and inference configuration side).

What I'll do next:
- Share a short commercial worksheet with scenarios (attached: redwood-econ-worksheet.xlsx) showing 12-month reserved pricing with a price-match band and an optional migration credit bucket.
- Loop in our runtime engineering lead (Marcus) and our solutions architect (Karthik) to run a quick compatibility checklist against your Llama-derived stack.

Questions for you (quick):
1) Are the quantized checkpoints standard int8 or using custom kernel-friendly packing?
2) Can you share a small sample model binary (or a test endpoint) we can validate against in us-west-2?
3) Do you require encrypted inference (HSM/KMS) or is TLS-only acceptable for now?

Operational notes:
- We aim for hot-swap migrations where KV caches are warmed in parallel; typical customer cutovers with zero customer-visible downtime take 2–6 hours of internal engineering work and an automated routing flip.
- For tight windows (00:00–03:00 PT), we recommend running a staged shadowing pass 48 hours before the planned cutover.

If you approve, I'll draft a one-page commercial anchor and a migration runbook, then set up a 30-min technical call with Marcus and Karthik.

Cheers,
Mina Haddad
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
mina_haddad@redwood.ai | +1-415-555-0123

Attachment: redwood-econ-worksheet.xlsx (Excel, 85 KB)

Ellie / Finance team — looping in a short commercial anchor and a migration checklist so you have something to review internally.

Commercial anchor (high level):
- 12-month Reserved Commitment: 2.5M runtime credits across supported families
- Price-match: Redwood will match incumbent effective blended rate up to a 20% band below our list for the first 6 months, subject to signed SLA addendum and committed quantity.
- Migration credit: Up to $60k in engineering credits applied as invoice credit over the first 3 billing cycles for verified migration milestones (shadowing, cutover, rollback test).
- Early termination: standard committed spend protections apply; we can add a 60-day exit clause for trial period with a reduced commitment level.

Technical & migration checklist (summary):
- Model compatibility: Marcus to validate custom packing; expected conversion effort 0–12 engineer-days depending on kernel rework.
- Networking/residency: Redwood dedicated endpoints in us-west-2 with customer VPC peering and optional transit gateway for minimal latency.
- Cutover plan: 48–72h staged shadowing, KV cache warm-up, incremental traffic ramp, final routing flip during your lowest load window, automated rollback plan documented.
- Security: TLS in validation; KMS/HSM integration in production (lead time ~2–3 weeks for key provisioning).

Attachments: draft-term-sheet.pdf (PDF, 42 KB) — includes pricing table and milestone definitions.

Next steps I propose:
1) Marcus / Karthik run a quick validation call with your engineering team this week (30 min).
2) If validation looks good, Finance and I will align on which migration milestones unlock the credit amounts and finalize the anchor.
3) We prepare a short DocuSign for the anchor and the SLA addendum to move forward.

If you want to shorten cycles, I'm happy to put up an internal approval request for an aggressive match (subject to product validation) to give you symmetry on timing with incumbent offers.

Best,
Mina
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
